description: ML failure modes decomposed. The specific ways trained models fail, and why each failure is inherent to the training paradigm rather than a fixable bug. Hallucination, adversarial examples, distribution shift, calibration breakdown, catastrophic forgetting, mode collapse, dataset contamination, spurious correlations.

sub_mechanisms.name: hallucination_pattern_matching
sub_mechanisms.definition: LLM generates plausible-sounding falsehoods. Fabricated citations, made-up facts, wrong dates.
sub_mechanisms.why: Training optimises for plausibility (probability under model distribution), not truth. Plausible-sounding outputs are statistically what the model is for. Truth is not an objective in pretraining.

sub_mechanisms.name: RAG_grounding
sub_mechanisms.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: search relevant docs; provide to model; model cites.
sub_mechanisms.why: Mitigates hallucination by providing actual context. Cost: retrieval quality + cite-without-hallucinate is still hard. Doesn't fundamentally fix the issue — model can still mis-attribute or fabricate from context.

sub_mechanisms.name: adversarial_perturbation_vision
sub_mechanisms.definition: Imperceptibly modified image causes wrong classification. Goodfellow 2014.
sub_mechanisms.why: Network decision boundary doesn't align with semantic boundary. Gradient direction reveals exact perturbation. Universal: works on every architecture. Network's 'understanding' differs from human's.

sub_mechanisms.name: jailbreak_prompt_engineering
sub_mechanisms.definition: Adversarial prompts bypassing safety: DAN, Sydney, roleplay, encoded instructions, prefix injection.
sub_mechanisms.why: Safety training shallow: token-pattern matching. Prompts that don't match training patterns slip through. Each generation of safety training spawns new jailbreaks. Universal: jailbreaks work across models.

sub_mechanisms.name: distribution_shift_calibration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Model trained on distribution A, deployed on distribution B. Accuracy + confidence calibration both break.
sub_mechanisms.why: Test set ≠ production. Common in production: data drift, new user populations, adversarial inputs. ML systems are brittle to OOD. The substrate's symbolic knowledge doesn't have this — facts don't shift.

sub_mechanisms.name: calibration_breakdown
sub_mechanisms.definition: Model confident on wrong answers. P(correct | conf=0.9) ≠ 0.9 under shift.
sub_mechanisms.why: Trained calibration only holds in distribution. Out-of-distribution: confidences become misleading. Critical for decision systems. Mitigation: temperature scaling, conformal prediction.

sub_mechanisms.name: catastrophic_forgetting_continual
sub_mechanisms.definition: Train on task A then B. Performance on A drops to near-random.
sub_mechanisms.why: Weights overwritten by gradient descent on task B. Network's representations restructured for new task. Inherent to SGD with shared weights. Mitigations: EWC, replay, LoRA (frozen base).

sub_mechanisms.name: mode_collapse_GAN
sub_mechanisms.definition: Generative model produces narrow output distribution. GAN converges to small set of outputs.
sub_mechanisms.why: Training instability. Generator finds outputs that fool discriminator + repeats. Diffusion models more stable but exhibit lesser version. Quality vs diversity tradeoff in all generative.

sub_mechanisms.name: dataset_contamination
sub_mechanisms.definition: Test set leaks into training data. Inflated metrics; misleading reports.
sub_mechanisms.why: Web-scale pretraining: hard to verify exclusion of standard benchmarks. GSM-8K, HumanEval may be in training data of various LLMs. Many published benchmark results suspect.

sub_mechanisms.name: spurious_correlations
sub_mechanisms.definition: Model learns correlation that's not causally relevant. Cow on grass classified as 'cow'; on beach: 'dog' (in some image classifiers).
sub_mechanisms.why: Loss minimised by any working signal, including spurious. Without explicit causal structure, can't distinguish. Standard problem; affects deployment robustness.

sub_mechanisms.name: data_leakage_in_training
sub_mechanisms.definition: Test labels leak into features during preprocessing. Or future information leaks back in time-series.
sub_mechanisms.why: Subtle: feature engineering can leak info. Standard cause of suspiciously-high training metrics that fail in production. Best practice: strict separation; even validation set must be untouched by feature engineering.

sub_mechanisms.name: benchmark_overfitting
sub_mechanisms.definition: Industry optimises for visible benchmarks; benchmarks no longer measure real capability.
sub_mechanisms.why: Models tuned to MMLU, GSM-8K, HumanEval. Benchmark scores increase faster than 'real' capability. Goodhart's law at industry scale.

derivation_rules.name: hallucination_inherent_to_probabilistic_generation
derivation_rules.why: Loss function rewards token-by-token plausibility. No truth signal. Model outputs what training distribution likes — which often is not what's true. RAG + structured knowledge (substrate's approach) provide alternatives.

derivation_rules.name: adversarial_examples_universal
if: network learned a function not equal to the human concept
derivation_rules.why: Different function = different decision boundary. Gradient ascent on input reveals boundary location. Universal across architectures, datasets. Symptom of statistical fit vs symbolic understanding.

derivation_rules.name: distribution_shift_compounds_in_production
if: deployed model sees inputs from distribution different from training
derivation_rules.why: ML systems are interpolators trained on a snapshot. Production data drifts: new users, new behaviours, new fraud patterns. Continuous retraining + monitoring is the operational practice. The substrate's symbolic knowledge doesn't drift.

derivation_rules.name: benchmark_contamination_invalidates_results
if: test data is in the model's training data
then: benchmark scores measure memorisation, not capability
derivation_rules.why: Web-scale pretraining likely includes published benchmarks. Reported gains may be from data leakage. Hard to verify; even self-reported tests suspect. The credibility crisis of current ML benchmarks.

derivation_rules.name: spurious_correlations_brittle_to_environment
then: it fails when correlation breaks in deployment
derivation_rules.why: Cow-on-grass classifier fails on cow-on-beach. Without causal structure, model can't distinguish background-of-class from class-itself. The substrate's explicit knowledge has causal structure built in via rule chains.
